completedAssessment: Bulk ASCII casing and byte-range whitespace scanning already exist; do not propose per-character string removal as missing.
Dictionary segments already share one probe and prevalidated native storage. Repeated integer-bound checks are not established as dominant removable work.
Unpublished machine integers already use final slots and exact promotion. The measured CSV sources use integer cents.
Tuple construction still materializes scalar objects into object arrays. Lazy tuple storage alone would often move boxing to the next subscript, while widening reference-heavy arrays.

tupleCandidate.hypothesis: End-to-end typed tuple aggregate transport could remove intermediate integer boxes and object-array payloads in per-record collection construction.
workToDisplace: PyTuple object-array backing for affected aggregate construction
Object-only tuple subscript transport when an immediate closed arithmetic consumer can avoid observation
semanticAcceptance: Stable repeated-item/alias identity through indexing, iteration, repetition and concatenation
Named tuples, equality/hash/repr, errors and evaluation order unchanged
Exact promotion and custom-index/protocol behavior preserved; no replay through fallback
Retained aliases/results and replacement peaks funded; refusal before allocation/mutation
Current cancellation and cleanup, genuine suspension and managed stack preserved
risks: Borrowed unboxed element identity may require more machinery than the saved storage justifies
Current source samples do not establish tuple construction as a dominant removable stage
tupleCandidate.boundedNext: Attribute tuple/scalar allocations and transport in an existing complete CSV script before selecting this larger redesign. Stop if no material whole-script target appears; keep reference-heavy text/JSON controls. No new identity ledger, universal tagged-value rewrite or narrow opcode series.
